title: Kong API Gateway Request Path
summary: Requests pass through Kong's plugin pipeline before reaching upstream services; configuration comes from PostgreSQL or declarative files applied by decK in CI.

nodes.label: API Client
nodes.detail: Sends HTTPS requests to the gateway with a token or API key. It never talks to upstream services directly.

nodes.label: Kong Data Plane
nodes.detail: Proxies traffic using routes and services held in memory. Runs each request through the plugin pipeline: authentication, rate limiting, transformation, logging.

nodes.label: Plugin Pipeline
nodes.detail: Plugins run in phases (access, header_filter, log). Typical order: authentication, rate limiting, request transformer, then logging on the response path.

nodes.label: Upstream Service A
nodes.detail: A backend service registered as a Kong Service. Kong load balances across its targets and runs active or passive health checks.

nodes.label: Upstream Service B
nodes.detail: Another backend behind a separate route. Different routes can apply different plugin sets.

nodes.label: Admin API
nodes.detail: REST API for managing services, routes, consumers and plugins. Should be restricted to internal networks and protected by RBAC.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.detail: Holds gateway configuration in database mode. Data planes cache it locally so request handling does not query the database.

nodes.label: deck
nodes.detail: CLI that diffs and syncs a declarative YAML file against Kong. Run from CI so gateway config is reviewed and versioned like code.

nodes.label: Git + CI
nodes.detail: Gateway configuration lives in Git. A pipeline validates the file and runs decK sync after merge.

steps.title: Client sends request
steps.text: The client calls a public hostname; Kong matches it to a route by host, path and method.

steps.title: Plugins run in order
steps.text: Authentication and rate-limit plugins execute first; a failure returns 401 or 429 without touching the upstream.

steps.title: Proxy to upstream
steps.text: Kong selects a healthy target using load balancing and forwards the request to the matching service.

steps.title: Config reviewed in Git
steps.text: Route and plugin changes are committed as declarative YAML and validated by the CI pipeline.

steps.title: decK syncs the gateway
steps.text: decK diffs the file against live state and applies changes through the Admin API into the datastore.

steps.title: Data planes pick up config
steps.text: Data planes receive updated configuration and apply it without dropping connections.
